Factorization H(t)=3sqrt3(1+ut)(1+vt), u+v=2 and uv=1/sqrt3, plus strict Newton inequalities for unequal positive repeated entries, proves the normalized sequence strictly decreases past the first index, and its end signs prove a unique cutoff. The exact k=2 formula proves all-dimensional ridge validity. Standalone exact quadratic-field script checks 1860 finite coefficient comparisons without being used to prove infinity.

value.rationale: Question 5.5 of the new Vaaler surface paper asks for the valid codimension range of skeleton cube bounds. This theorem completely determines it, and every sharp skeletal minimum, for products of admissible planar triangles in all even dimensions. The nontrivial strict crossing means no later return to validity, and the n=4 example separates the conjectured ridge index from the next skeleton. Equality and failure witnesses are exact.
